controllingSource.title: User architecture correction
controllingSource.summary: Aura has seven nested horn tori with programmable facets. Patterns are grouped and selected in stacks for AI computation that creates documents and websites. Corrections produce revised patterns and groups, then new chosen stacks and further runs. The cycle operates across multiple selves and internal private/secret and external public domains with different encryption and permissions.

sourceBasis.authorship: Entity names, fields, stages, contracts and all example records below are new design synthesis. They are not claimed to occur verbatim in the source documents.

definition: Aura is the user-defined seven-nested-horn-torus pattern architecture with programmable facets and an iterative pattern-group → chosen stack → permitted AI computation → artifact → correction → regrouping cycle across selected self frames and access domains.

geometry.indexing: Shell indices 1–7 follow the Root-to-Crown chakra correspondence. The current Matrix profile establishes 12 × 24 = 288 base facets per shell. Geometry coordinates and semantic assignments must reference their explicit geometry version; future profile changes require a new version rather than changing historical addresses.
geometry.functionalAssignment: The seven tori represent the etheric Aura’s chakras. Their practical themes guide pattern and question organisation. A torus, self, observer and access domain each have a separate role.
geometry.placementRule: A programmable facet has a base address and an outward stack of layers. Each layer can carry records, instructions, required JSON and assets. Placement may remain unassigned in this illustrative example; it is never inferred from a pattern label.
geometry.commonPinch: Seven nested horn-torus shells with R = r and a shared pinch; see HG1. Geometry is separate from cognitive labels and access domains.

currentMatrixProfile.scope: Current Matrix Studio address profile, not a claim that these numbers define cognitive capacity.

geometry.sideVsDomain: Inside/outside are geometric address spaces. An outside facet is not automatically public, and an inside facet is not encrypted. The separate access-domain field controls the proposed permissions.

entities.name: pattern
entities.purpose: A reusable, provenance-bearing unit: concept, relationship, observation, instruction, example, question or explicitly labelled hypothesis.
invariants: A pattern may belong to many groups; a group may contain many patterns. Membership is a relationship, not a copy that silently forks the pattern.
A pattern is not automatically true because it is selected or frequently retrieved.
Revision creates a new version; historical versions remain addressable under their original access controls.

entities.name: patternGroupRevision
entities.purpose: A versioned association of patterns with a stated grouping rationale, relationships and unresolved alternatives.
invariants: Membership records pin pattern ID/revision and state the role or reason.
A group has no automatic top-to-bottom order; readingRule is explicit or unresolved.
Regrouping may add, remove, split, combine or relate memberships without erasing source patterns.

entities.name: facet
entities.purpose: An addressable programmable base facet with an outward layer stack; each selected layer binding prepares or performs a bounded operation.
invariants: Geometry placement does not grant data or tool access.
A binding identifies its actual implementation or says design-only.
A facet may present several selectable binding versions; each run pins exactly the one it uses.
Each outward layer pins its address, record selections, instructions, required JSON, assets, program binding and output contract. Retain spatial order and layer boundaries in export and execution.

entities.name: stack
entities.purpose: Either an outward facet-layer stack, or an explicitly typed compute composition selecting and sequencing one or more facet stacks. The two levels are distinct.
invariants: kind is facet-layer-stack or compute-composition. A facet-layer-stack keeps torus/side/baseFacet/layer addresses and per-layer records, instructions, required JSON and assets. A compute-composition selects those stacks/layers without erasing their provenance or order.
Each step names a selected pattern/group revision or facet binding and its input/output dependencies.
Order is local to the stack, not a universal order imposed on the source matrix.
A changed group does not silently change a saved or running stack.
A stack requests capabilities; it cannot grant them.

entities.name: run
entities.purpose: One bounded execution or explicitly labelled authored rehearsal of a selected stack.
invariants: Resolve and freeze actual inputs before compute; group labels alone are insufficient.
Record model/program version, budgets, tool calls and actual timings when executed; unknown values stay unknown.
Child workers receive scoped inputs and capabilities for their task, not a whole parent archive.
A design trace is not reported as an actual model run.

entities.name: artifactRevision
entities.purpose: A document, website, diagram, lesson, code output or other concrete result with lineage and its own review/release state.
invariants: Generating a public-intended draft does not publish it.
Derived content retains input restrictions until a specific permitted release projection is reviewed.
An external page cannot retrieve private or secret parent inputs through its lineage links.

entities.name: correction
entities.purpose: An attributed change request or dispute about a claim, pattern, grouping, stack, artifact or permission.
invariants: Observed behavior, participant meaning, reviewer inference and fictional feedback remain distinguishable.
A local correction does not silently become a rule about every self or context.
Corrections append lineage and can remain disputed or unresolved.

entities.name: selfFrame
entities.purpose: A selected representation of a person at a time, in a role or under explicitly named conditions.
invariants: Past, present, possible and constrained frames are separate from the three observers.
A speculative future frame is not evidence of future achievement.
Selecting another frame does not copy all answers or unlock its records.

entities.name: accessDomain
entities.purpose: An independently enforced data and capability boundary.
invariants: Private, secret and external-public permissions are independently checked.
Public readability does not confer editing, publishing, spending, messaging or tool authority.
No external-public worker inherits internal inputs, embeddings, logs, credentials or capabilities.

cycle.title: Frame the intended result
cycle.action: Name the purpose, artifact, selected self frames, audience and success evidence.
cycle.output: A mission contract with an output target and explicit access domain.

cycle.title: Select permitted evidence
cycle.action: Resolve authorised MVS entries, observer accounts, sources, existing artifacts and correction records.
cycle.output: A version-pinned input manifest, including absent or deliberately excluded information.

cycle.title: Form or choose pattern groups
cycle.action: Identify reusable units and grouping rationale; preserve ambiguous spatial readings and many-to-many membership.
cycle.output: Selected group revisions and unresolved alternatives.

cycle.title: Program or select facets
cycle.action: Choose the base facet and its outward layer stack; pin each layer’s records, instructions, required JSON, assets, program binding, tool scope and budget.
cycle.output: Facet binding references; design-only bindings remain labelled.

cycle.title: Choose the stack
cycle.action: Select one or more facet stacks, preserve their outward-layer recall/program sequence, and define explicit cross-facet transitions, dependencies, self-frame choices and review gates.
cycle.output: An immutable run manifest and dependency graph.

cycle.title: Compute and make
cycle.action: Run permitted AI/tool tasks to produce concrete documents, websites or other artifacts; independent jobs may overlap.
cycle.output: Artifact drafts plus actual execution or failure records. No automatic publication.

cycle.title: Encounter and correct
cycle.action: Inspect outputs and, where agreed, use them in a real task. Separate observed outcomes, interpretations, participant meaning and fictional rehearsal.
cycle.output: Targeted corrections with evidence, scope and dispositions.

cycle.title: Revise and regroup
cycle.action: Revise affected patterns, create group revisions, split or link groups and update facet bindings where needed.
cycle.output: New addressable revisions and a dependency impact list; earlier runs remain unchanged.

cycle.title: Choose the next stack
cycle.action: Explicitly select revised versions, compare a meaningful alternative and state what result could change the choice.
cycle.output: The next run contract or a documented decision to stop, defer or retain disagreement.

accessDomains.capabilities: Only the particular read, compute, write and export operations granted for the current purpose.
accessDomains.keyScope: A protected private-domain key/access boundary; implementation and key management remain to be designed.
accessDomains.inheritance: No secret access by default; no automatic public release.

accessDomains.visibility: internal, more narrowly authorised secret material
accessDomains.capabilities: Explicit secret-domain authority for each permitted principal and operation; presence in the same Aura is insufficient.
accessDomains.keyScope: A separately controlled secret-domain key/access boundary; a private-domain grant or key must not unlock it.
accessDomains.inheritance: No automatic inclusion in private-domain retrieval, model context, training, logs or outputs.

accessDomains.visibility: publicly released or wholly authored public-safe material
accessDomains.capabilities: Fewer capabilities: read selected public material and, when separately granted, prepare scoped drafts. No internal authority is inherited.
accessDomains.keyScope: Public payload need not be confidential; integrity, provenance and separate publication credentials still require real controls.
accessDomains.inheritance: No private/secret input, key, hidden lineage content or tool authority. Public read is not publication permission.

encryption.status: Requirements only. The present static site and local pattern walkthrough do not implement these cryptographic domains.
requirements: Protect private and secret content in storage and transit under their respective independently controlled boundaries.
Manage keys outside public files, model prompts, shared browser storage and exported public examples. Define creation, access, rotation, recovery and revocation responsibilities.
Check both access policy and cryptographic key authority before decryption; a visual padlock or geometry layer is insufficient.
Limit plaintext exposure to the authorised worker and task. Define temporary-file, cache, embedding, log, crash-report and backup handling for each domain.
Treat group memberships, links, titles and correction metadata as potentially revealing; a public graph must not expose forbidden internal structure.
Preserve input restrictions on derived artifacts. A public release requires an explicit approved projection and inspection for unintended disclosure.
Record what revocation can prevent going forward and what cannot be recalled from earlier authorised exports or recipients.
Verify denied-access behavior, key separation, recovery and export boundaries before claiming the architecture is operational.
encryption.algorithmChoice: No cryptographic algorithm, product or deployment implementation is chosen by this illustrative document.

implementationBoundary.existing: Static workbook, source catalogue, authored curricula and limited local observer/task prototypes described elsewhere in this repository.
implementationBoundary.newDesign: Seven-torus pattern bindings, general pattern/group/stack data model, corrective regrouping engine, integrated self/access domain enforcement and cryptographic storage described here.
notClaimed: Training model weights merely by regrouping patterns
Encrypted storage supplied by labels or browser saving
Real participant results from the fictional example

stackDistinction.facetStack: A spatial stack growing outward from one base facet: ordered layers addressed by torus + side + base facet + layer. Each layer has its own records, instructions, required JSON and assets. Outward order can define recall/program order.
stackDistinction.computeComposition: A deliberately selected version-pinned sequence over one or more facet stacks or selected layer addresses, with explicit transitions, operations, dependencies, inputs and outputs. It preserves the spatial stack addresses and ordering rather than flattening all material into a generic prompt.
stackDistinction.patternGroup: A reusable many-to-many semantic association. Its members may be bound at multiple facet layers. A group is not automatically a spatial stack or an executable programme.

matrixBridge.skillExport: SKILL.md containing the same manifest and interpretation instructions
matrixBridge.currentBehavior: The Matrix browser navigates, recalls attached records and handles timing. It does not execute external AI instructions as tool calls, install the exported skill or schedule background automation.
matrixBridge.runnerBoundary: A separate authorised runner must resolve addresses, verify versions and access, interpret instructions, perform permitted compute, validate output and return artifact/correction references. This document defines that proposed bridge; it does not implement it.
matrixBridge.recordBoundary: Matrix table allocation currently copies records into addresses. The reference model here additionally requires explicit lineage between a source pattern and each placed instance; it does not pretend existing copies already synchronise.

patterns.content: A lesson should help its learner produce and improve one chosen artifact, under a named purpose.
A labelled worked example can connect an explanation to the concrete document and website it creates.
Matching a term to a label provides evidence of recognition; it does not establish independent application.
A chosen stack pins group revisions, facet-layer addresses, binding versions and output dependencies.
Every example and its feedback remain labelled fictional until a real encounter supplies separate evidence.
Environment, character attention and narrator accounts are selected evidence; participant meaning stays separately attributed.
Artifact revisions name their source selections and the corrections that changed them.
The learner can choose a low-stakes task or use the supplied invented scenario.
A public-intended draft is distinct from an authorised publication action.
A learner demonstrates application by choosing and revising a stack for a new task, explaining the change after feedback.
The page separates Inputs, Create draft, Inspect result and Revise, with visible current versions.
Show seven nested horn tori and programmable outward facet layers without assigning invented cognitive names to the tori.
A public demonstration cannot access private or secret records or acquire publication authority.
Inside/outside geometric addressing does not change access domain; public execution must fail a request for an unauthorised internal record.
